A merchant and a farmer travelled together. They needed to pass through an uninhabited forest.
A merchant and a farmer were travelling together. They needed to pass through a forest with no trace/whiff/mist of people.
After the bear approached, it saw the farmer lying on the ground. It came over to sniff him with its nose and circled around him for a long time.
After the bear got close, it saw the farmer lying on the ground and came over to sniff using its nose, circling around him for a long time.
But the farmer hugged the tree trunk and just couldn't climb up, so he had no choice but to quickly lie on the ground and pretend to be dead.
But the farmer hugging the tree just couldn't climb up, he was forced to quickly lie on the ground and play dead.
It was a dangerous area, so they made an agreement that no matter what danger they encountered, both of them would help each other.
It was a dangerous place so they made a pact that no matter what danger they experienced they would help each other.

Knowing that the bear had gone, the merchant only then came down from up in the tree. the farmer also got up. The merchant then asked the farmer: "Friend, when the great bear was leaning over you just now, what did he whisper in your ear?"
Not long after they walked into the forest, danger arrived—a big bear was walking toward them from up ahead.

Not until the big bear had walked far away did the merchant come down from the tree, and the farmer climbed up from the ground too. The merchant then asked the farmer, "My friend, what did the big bear whisper right next to your ear just now?"
Nǐ de ěr páng gēn nǐ shuōle xiē shénme ya
Pretending not to care at all, the farmer said calmly and unhurriedly, "The big bear didn't actually tell me any secrets. It only told me not to make friends with untrustworthy people next time!"
Seeing the bear walking toward them, the merchant abandoned the farmer and climbed the tree alone to hide.
Shāngrén dòngzuò mǐnjié, tā gǎnkuài páshàng zuìjìn de dà shù duǒ qǐlái.
Speaking in a measured, unhurried manner
The bear thought the farmer was truly a dead person, so it walked away. Because bears do not eat dead people.
The farmer closed his eyes tightly, held his breath, and kept perfectly still.
The farmer shut his eyes tightly, held his breath, and did not move at all.
The farmer, pretending not to care, evenly replied: "Actually, the great bear didn't speak any secrets, he only told me that next time don't make friends with untrustworthy people."
The great bear presumed the farmer really was a dead person, and soon walked away, because bears be like don't eat dead people yo!
The merchant acted with agility, quickly climbing the nearest large tree to hide.
The merchant moved quickly and nimbly; he immediately climbed up the nearest large tree to hide.
They hadn't gone far through the forest when danger suddenly was upon them. A large bear was walking towards them from up ahead.

This sentence contains two "lin" words. In the first half of the sentence, lín is the character 林.  The Word: 树林 i.e. shùlín with literal meaning 树 /shù / tree + 林 / lín / forest/grove.  Character Origin: the character 林, it is literally made of two "tree" characters 木 = mù standing side-by-side. In the second half of the sentence, lín is the character 临 [traditional: 臨]. The Word: 来临 / láilín has literal meaning 来 / lái / to come + 临 / to arrive/draw near. Usage: 临 on its own means "to be close to," "to face," or "to arrive." When combined as 来临, it means "to arrive" or "to approach." It is highly formal and usually used for abstract things, e.g., danger approaching, winter arriving, or a new era coming.
Tāmen zǒujìn shùlín bù jiǔ, wēixiǎn jiù láilín le —— yì zhī dà xióng cóng qiánmiàn cháo tā men zǒu lái.

nodes.name: kě nóngfū bàozhe shù gàn jiùshì pá bú shàngqù, tā zhǐhǎo gǎnkuài tǎng zài dìshang zhuāngsǐ.
nodes.tooltip: This sentence starts with 可/kě is used here as a shortened, spoken form of 但是/dànshì or 可是/kěshì, meaning "but" or "however". Gemini informs: what makes this sentence work so well is the relationship between 可/kě at the beginning and 就是/jiùshì in the middle: 可 flags to the listener: "Pay attention, a problem is coming!" 说明/就是 emphasizes the total frustration or helplessness of the situation: "He tried, but he just couldn't do it." If you were reading this fable out loud, that initial 可 is the exact moment the tension spikes for the character! · The three characters 干就是 gàn jiù shì seem to form two words, either gànjiù and jiùshì with different meanings. Gemini points out the role of jiùshì to mean "just", while the translation suggests that gànjiù/just do it is more appropriate. So these three altogether form a hybrid or emphasis where the binding is ambiguous.

一位商人和一位农夫结伴同行，他们要经过一个没有人烟的树林。
一只大熊从前面朝他们走来
他们走进树林不久，危险就来临了——一只大熊从前面朝他们走来。
他只好赶快躺在地上装死
他赶快爬上最近大叔躲起来
你的耳旁跟你说了些什么呀
农夫紧闭双眼，屏住呼吸，一动也不动。
农夫装作毫不在乎的样子，不紧不慢地说："大熊倒是没和我说什么秘密，它只是告诉我，下次不要再和没有信用的人交朋友/ ！"
可农夫抱着树干就是爬不上去
可农夫抱着树干就是爬不上去，他只好赶快躺在地上装死。
商人动作敏捷，他赶快爬上最近的大树躲起来。
商人听了，羞愧地低下了头。
商人看到熊向他们走来，便扔下农夫，一个人爬到树上躲藏起来。
大熊以为农夫真的是个死人，就走开了。因为熊是不吃死人的。
熊走近后，看见躺在地上的农夫，就过来用鼻子闻，并围绕着他绕了半天。
直到大熊走远了，商人才从树上下来，农夫也爬了起来。商人就问农夫："朋友,大熊刚才伏在你的耳旁跟你说了些什么呀？"
那里是危险地带，所以他们约好了，无论遇见什么危险，两个人都要相互帮助。
